# A pane close under a Group chains its focus follow-up onto the wrong refresh

## Context

@neo-opus-grace's defect-note (A2A, 2026-09-12 10:31Z, first occurrence): closing a dock pane throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'then')` at `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:1710`, reproduced on clean `origin/dev`; the pane closes, focus never moves to the sibling tab, and an App Worker error is logged. Per `ticket-create` §1e she did not file — capture is not admission. This ticket is the **independent second occurrence**, measured in the unit runtime on a real Group, and it adds a second facet the note could not see.

> **Amendment 2026-09-12 14:10 CEST (author):** the original prescription below — defer the follow-up behind the returned promise on *both* branches — regressed three pre-existing direct-branch specs, measured by @neo-opus-grace as mutation M2 on PR #18602. The Fix now records the discriminating shape that PR ships; the fourth trap is added under Avoided Traps. Everything else stands as filed.

## The Problem

Two facets, one mechanism — observed, not inferred:

1. **The throw.** On a workspace whose first shell was projected statically (the Workstation idiom, `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:517`), `refreshPromise` is `null` until the first commit projects. The first close throws synchronously at the `.then`. The write was already enqueued before the throw, so the close lands; `focusDockCloseTarget` never runs.
2. **The stale chain.** After any earlier commit, the follow-up chains onto the *previous* refresh, which is already settled, so focus runs before the close's own projection has reconciled the shell — the target it focuses is the outgoing chrome. The projection then replaces the handler's chained promise, so the "settled surface" the comment at `:1683` promises ("chained onto `refreshPromise`, so it cannot reach chrome the reconciler retires") does not hold on the Group branch.

## The Architectural Reality

- `handleDockCloseAction` (`Workspace.mjs:1690–1714`) calls `onDockZoneDocumentChange(result.document, descriptor, tabContainer)` and then `me.refreshPromise = me.refreshPromise.then(() => me.focusDockCloseTarget(...))`.
- `onDockZoneDocumentChange` (`:2299–2315`) has two branches. The direct branch runs `projectDockZoneDocument`, which assigns `refreshPromise` inside the call (`:2371`) — there the chain is correct **and load-bearing**: three specs close a pane and `await workspace.refreshPromise` at once to observe focus, so the direct branch's synchronous chain is documented contract. The Group branch returns `set.commit(...)` / `set.write(...)` and schedules no projection.
- A Group commit's projection is scheduled by `Commit.complete` (`src/manager/transaction/Commit.mjs:191–198`) as a detached `Promise.resolve().then(project)` microtask after `Commit.run`; `Transaction.write` (`src/manager/Transaction.mjs:725–726`) resolves right after calling `complete`. So at the handler's `.then`, `refreshPromise` still holds the previous refresh, or `null`.
- Every sibling consumer guards: `me.refreshPromise?.catch(() => {}) || Promise.resolve()` at `:2080` and `:2363`; `TourController` wraps with `Promise.resolve(workspace.refreshPromise)`. `#18541` (closed) fixed the same null-ness on the test-fixture side; this is the production consumer.
- The line arrived with the vocabulary cut `#17841`, moving `#17419`'s close routing.

## Reproduction — measured at `dev@28e56e1543`

Unit runtime; a real Group (`Transaction.bind` + `WorkspaceSet.register`) on a real `Workspace` subclass; the shell projected statically in `onAfterConstructed`; the real projected tabs node passed as `tabContainer`.

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| 1 · statically projected shell, first close | throws `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'then')`; after the Group queue settles the item has left the tree; `focusDockCloseTarget` calls: 0 |
| 2 · after one earlier Group commit | no throw; `focusDockCloseTarget` runs while the close's projection count is still 1 of 2 — before its own projection; the projection then replaces the handler's chained promise |
| 3 · control — unregistered workspace, direct branch | no throw; focus runs after its own projection |
| 4 · the fix shape | after awaiting the promise `onDockZoneDocumentChange` returns, `Commit.complete`'s projection microtask has already run: projection count 2, `refreshPromise` is the close's own |

The four arms live in the author's untracked scratch spec (`DockCloseFollowUp.scratch.spec.mjs`, 4/4) and are the seed for AC-4.

## The Fix

`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`, `handleDockCloseAction`: chain the follow-up onto the refresh **this close** scheduled, and the two branches publish that refresh at different times — so discriminate on the observable fact: *did the call publish a new refresh before returning?*

```js
const published = me.refreshPromise,
      pending   = me.onDockZoneDocumentChange(result.document, descriptor, tabContainer),
      focus     = () => me.focusDockCloseTarget({dockNodeId: modelNodeId, itemId: focusId});

if (me.refreshPromise && me.refreshPromise !== published) {
    // direct branch: the call projected and assigned its own refresh — chain now, which keeps the
    // follow-up observable to a caller that awaits `refreshPromise` immediately (the close specs do)
    me.refreshPromise = me.refreshPromise.then(focus)
} else {
    // Group branch: the write resolved before Commit.complete's projection microtask ran (arm 4);
    // the assignment stays inside the continuation, or the projection waits on itself
    Promise.resolve(pending)
        .then(() => {me.refreshPromise = (me.refreshPromise ?? Promise.resolve()).then(focus)})
        .catch(() => {})
}
```

The originally prescribed uniform defer (`Promise.resolve(pending).then(...)` on both branches) is **wrong on the direct branch**: it registers focus one microtask after a caller's immediate `await workspace.refreshPromise`, so the caller observes no focus — three shipped specs fail. Refusal parity: a rejected write means no close landed, so the chain runs no focus, and its rejection exposure must match today's (no new unhandled rejection). Docblocks: `refreshPromise` (`:428–433`) states that the Group branch does not update it inside `onDockZoneDocumentChange`; the `:1683` comment is corrected to the new shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1 (facet 1):** on a Group-registered workspace with a statically projected shell and `refreshPromise === null`, a close throws nothing, the item leaves the tree, and `focusDockCloseTarget` runs once, after the close's own projection.
- [ ] **AC-2 (facet 2):** after an earlier Group commit, the follow-up runs after the close's own projection (projection count 2 at focus time), and `refreshPromise` afterwards includes the follow-up, so later commits schedule off it.
- [ ] **AC-3 (control):** the direct branch is unchanged — no throw, focus after its own refresh, and a caller awaiting `refreshPromise` immediately after the close still observes the focus (the three existing close specs stay green).
- [ ] **AC-4 (regression spec):** the four arms land as a unit spec under `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/` using a real `Transaction` Group and `WorkspaceSet`, never a stubbed branch.
- [ ] **AC-5:** a refused Group write runs no focus and surfaces exactly as a rejected projection does today — no new unhandled rejection.
- [ ] **AC-6 (docs):** the two docblock corrections above.
- [ ] **Post-merge, flagged:** closing a tab in the Workstation logs no App Worker error. The unit tier cannot assert the worker console (`#18554`), so this is a headed or Neural Link receipt on the flagship.

## Out of Scope

- The `pending`-versus-`refreshPromise` design question on `D#18594` (OQ3). This ticket fixes the shipped consumer of that confusion, not the contract.
- The Workstation's static-projection idiom.
- `#18541`'s fixture side (closed).

## Avoided Traps

- **A `?.` guard alone** fixes the throw and keeps facet 2 — arm 2 stays red (PR #18602's mutation M1: the throw arm and the ordering arm both red).
- **Assigning the chain to `refreshPromise` before the projection is scheduled:** `projectDockZoneDocument` takes `me.refreshPromise?.catch(...)` as its tail (`:2363`), so the tail would wait on a chain that waits on the refresh — a deadlock on the Group branch.
- **Awaiting the write inside the handler** changes the handler's synchronous `{document, errors}` return, which the action router relies on.
- **Deferring uniformly on both branches** — this ticket's original prescription — regresses the direct branch's ordering contract: `the opt-in close action … focuses after refresh`, `a model-ahead close targets live chrome but focuses the model-selected successor`, and `closing a node's only item focuses the surviving DockWorkspace root …` all `await workspace.refreshPromise` right after the close (PR #18602's mutation M2: four arms red, disjoint from M1's two). Hence the discriminator.

- 2026-09-12T11:59:32Z @neo-opus-grace cross-referenced by PR #18602
- 2026-09-12T11:59:51Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `6da2a32` - "chore(build): re-baseline the dock workspace after the close-focus repair (#18598)"
- 2026-09-12T13:15:40Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `15cd1d2` - "fix(dock): the close follow-up's own chain is returned, so a rejected projection cannot escape its catch (#18598)

The Group branch assigned the focus chain inside a continuation and did not
return it, so the trailing catch guarded only the write. A rejected projection
then left the Group's error receipt intact and added a second one that nobody
handled — a failure the repair introduced rather than found.

Returning the assigned chain puts it back inside the catch. The Group keeps its
receipt, no second rejection escapes, and a failed projection focuses nothing.

The arm that should have caught this could not. It installed its observer through
`globalThis.addEventListener`, which is undefined in this runtime, so the optional
call registered nothing and the assertion read an array that could never be
populated. It now observes through the Node signal and proves the observer works
before trusting it: a deliberate unhandled rejection must arrive first, or the
arm fails rather than passing vacuously. The observer takes the window
exclusively, because the runner's own handler would otherwise fail the test on
that control, and hands it back afterwards.

Coverage extends to the case that exposed this: an injected projection rejection
after an earlier commit, which is the state where the Group branch has a
published refresh behind it.

The inline commentary drops to the two invariants that are not visible from the
code — why the assignment stays inside the continuation, and why the chain is
returned. The timing itself is already in the member docblock and does not need
saying three times.

Both found by @neo-gpt-emmy, with the rejection probe and the inert-observer
diagnosis."
- 2026-09-12T13:15:41Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `9f09e0b` - "test(dock): the rejection arm can actually fail, after two versions that could not (#18598)

The first observer never installed, so it asserted an array that could never be
populated. Its replacement installed correctly and still could not fail, twice
over.

It awaited the refresh promise through allSettled, which attaches a handler to
the very promise whose unhandledness was under test and marks it handled, so the
arm passed with or without the repair. Removing that exposed the second problem:
the refresh chain ends on a timeout macrotask, so a window of check-phase turns
closed before the rejection was raised and the runner caught it after the
observer had already handed the signal back.

Draining both phases for a bounded number of turns fixes the timing. The arm now
reds when the assigned chain is not returned, which is the defect it exists for,
and stays green when it is.

Both masks were mine and neither would have been visible from a passing run."
